questions.question: 在执行清理操作时，您希望如何平衡「清理效果（释放更多空间）」与「数据安全（防止误删用户重要文件）」？

questions.recommendation: (Recommended) 采用保守的安全策略，默认只勾选绝对安全的临时缓存文件，敏感区域仅扫描提示而不默认勾选。
questions.recommendation_reason: 安全是清理类软件的生命线。任何一次误删对用户而言都是灾难性的，保守策略能最大限度降低误删风险，建立用户信任。

tensions.description: 极致的一键清理体验与复杂的文件确认流程之间的矛盾。

questions.recommendation: 系统提供公共课（数/英/政）细化标准计划，对专业课提供“通用教材页数/章节数拆分模板”，由用户输入总章节后等分生成框架。
questions.recommendation_reason: 这种混合方案开发成本低，能让专业课复习计划具备可操作性，避免冷启动流失。

options.impact: 几乎不增加后端架构复杂度，只需做前端样式适配，就能极大提高用户在自习室等场景下的使用频次和打卡率。
options.label: (Recommended) 核心以桌面端为主，但提供适配移动端浏览器的极简打卡/任务查看页面（Responsive Web Design）。

options.impact: 可以通过邮件唤醒用户，但用户仍然需要回到电脑端或使用桌面排版页面操作，可能存在打卡延迟。
options.label: 坚守仅桌面端浏览器，不提供任何移动端适配，但每天晚上通过邮件发送任务摘要和提醒。

options.impact: 开发最简单，但由于备考场景限制，用户流失和忘记打卡的风险极高，容易导致 MVP 指标失真。
options.label: 不做任何移动端适配和主动提醒，完全依赖用户主动在电脑上登录桌面端使用。

questions.question: 由于考研学生大部分时间在自习室/图书馆备考，桌面浏览器并不方便随时查看和打卡。MVP 阶段您倾向于如何解决这个备考场景痛点？
questions.reason: 若打卡不便，用户很容易因遗忘或懒于开电脑而放弃记录，导致“连续两周完成率”这一核心指标极难达成。
questions.recommendation: 核心以桌面端为主，但提供适配移动端浏览器的极简打卡/任务查看页面（Responsive Web Design）。
questions.recommendation_reason: 移动端浏览器自适应成本很低（同一套前端代码），但能完美覆盖学生在自习室“拿出手机看一眼、随手划掉已完成任务”的日常使用场景。

options.impact: 保证了复习总量不丢失，并能客观反映备考压力，符合“安静、鼓励”的心理调性。
options.label: (Recommended) 自动将延后任务平摊到后续所有周，当某周总时长超过用户设定的“每周可学习时长”时，在主页给出温和的进度赤字预警（如提示“建议本周额外学习3小时”）。

options.impact: 实现最简单，但容易导致后续某一周压力突然暴增，破坏计划的指导性。
options.label: 仅将延后任务无脑推迟到下一周，由下一周用户自己再次决定是否延后（滚动累积）。

options.impact: 将控制权完全交给用户，但交互步骤增多，且用户可能不知道如何科学分配。
options.label: 不进行自动分摊，当用户点击“延后”或“拆分”时，弹出二次弹窗引导用户手动选择重新分配到哪一周。

questions.question: 当用户将某项任务“延后”或“拆分”时，您希望后续的复习计划进行怎样的自动重排？
questions.reason: 考研复习具有明确的截止日期（总量固定）。延后任务必须妥善重排，否则会导致后续计划脱节。
questions.recommendation: 自动将延后任务平摊到后续所有周，当某周总时长超过用户设定的“每周可学习时长”时，在主页给出温和的进度赤字预警（如提示“建议本周额外学习3小时”）。
questions.recommendation_reason: 这种平摊预警机制既有计划指导性，又不会给用户造成立即的压迫感，鼓励用户逐步追赶进度。

risks: 【专业课黑洞风险】由于自命题专业课大纲无法标准化，若强制由用户手动录入大纲，初始化成本过高会导致用户在第一步流失；若不支持专业课，则失去“一站式考研计划”核心卖点。
【移动场景缺失风险】考研学生核心场景（自习室）多使用移动端，纯桌面端极易导致遗忘打卡、更新不及时，从而使 MVP 连续两周完成率验证指标失真。
【过度延后崩盘风险】如果没有对“延后”任务的总上限或警示约束，用户频繁延后任务会导致后期计划雪崩式堆积，失去使用信心。
【缺少触达唤醒风险】缺乏邮件/短信等主动通知渠道，若用户忘记登录桌面网页，将直接导致连续两周打卡失败，无法验证 MVP 价值。
unknowns: 针对成百上千种专业课（尤其是自命题）科目，系统该如何获取大纲并科学生成计划？
任务被“延后”或“拆分”后，后续周的复习量与可学习时长上限发生冲突时，系统重新分摊的数学模型是什么？
MVP 验证指标中“连续两周完成任务”的具体完成百分比阈值（如需达到本周任务的 80% 还是 100% 才算完成）尚未定义。
备考核心场景（自习室/图书馆）下，仅有桌面浏览器版是否会导致用户打卡记录极其滞后或流失？

assumptions: Students have reliable internet access on their desktop/laptop computers during their dedicated study review times.
The postgraduate exam date is a fixed target in the future and does not change once entered by the user.
Weekly study hour budgets remain relatively stable week-to-week unless manually adjusted by the student.
candidates: Pre-loaded postgraduate syllabus templates for standard subjects (Politics, English, Math, common majors) to simplify onboarding.
A structured weekly review/re-planning prompt (e.g., every Sunday) to help students reflect and adjust the next week's load.
A graceful buffer mechanism that visually groups deferred tasks separately to avoid cluttering the active week's dashboard.
confirmed: Target audience: Chinese college students preparing for the postgraduate entrance exam (考研).
Supported language: Chinese only for the first version.
Supported platform: Desktop browsers only for the first version.
Onboarding inputs: Exam date, subjects, weekly study hours, and current foundation.
Core feature: Generation of a week-by-week adjustable review plan.
Homepage elements: Current week's tasks, completion progress, and countdown to the exam.
Task detail actions: Mark as complete, defer, or split.
Identity/Storage: Email registration, cloud data storage, and cross-device login capability.
UX/UI style: Quiet, encouraging, mature (not childish), combining calendar and to-do list concepts.
MVP exclusions: Social features, course marketplace, AI chat, and native mobile apps.
Validation cohort: 20 students for the initial trial.
Validation success metric: The percentage of students who complete their tasks for two consecutive weeks.

gaps.dependency: Task detail actions (defer/split)
gaps.impact: If deferred tasks are simply dumped into the next week without redistribution rules, the student will experience compounding planning debt, leading to abandonment.
gaps.reason: No flow is defined for how the system recalculates or redistributes tasks when they are deferred or split.

gaps.dependency: Plan generation logic
gaps.impact: If users must enter every study task manually, onboarding friction will be extremely high. If templates are pre-defined, the tool must manage syllabus accuracy.
gaps.reason: It is not specified whether task lists are generated from a pre-defined subject syllabus template or if they are entirely user-inputted.

options.impact: Maintains a realistic and achievable schedule, preventing the feeling of accumulated debt while keeping the student in control.
options.label: (Recommended) Weekly Re-planning Checkpoint: Prompt the student at the end of the week to manually adjust their weekly study hours, shift the target scope, or extend the review duration to absorb the deferred tasks.

options.impact: Simplifies application logic but heavily risks demotivating the student as their weekly task load compounds.
options.label: Automatic Rollover: Push all incomplete tasks to the next week automatically, increasing that week's daily workload.

options.impact: Keeps the daily schedule constant but might result in the student failing to cover all exam material before the fixed exam date.
options.label: Deadline Warning: Keep the weekly workload constant but warn the user that they will not finish the syllabus before the exam unless they manually adjust their pace.

questions.question: How should the tool handle plan recalculation when a student consistently falls behind, defers, or splits tasks?
questions.reason: If the system simply rolls over unfinished tasks without a clear renegotiation flow, it will create 'planning debt' that demotivates students. This directly threatens your primary success metric (consecutive 2-week task completion).
questions.recommendation: Implement a weekly re-planning checkpoint that prompts the user to re-negotiate their plan (e.g., adjust weekly hours, extend timelines, or downscope sub-topics) rather than letting tasks pile up.
questions.recommendation_reason: This keeps the plan realistic and respects user autonomy without childish gamification.

options.impact: Minimizes onboarding drop-off, but provides less precise plan calibration.
options.label: (Recommended) Phase-based Self-assessment Checklist: Select from broad stages for each subject (e.g., 'Zero foundation', 'First-round review finished', 'Doing mock tests').

options.impact: More objective, but requires students to have taken a recent mock exam or practice set prior to using the tool.
options.label: Target Score Gap Entry: Input target score vs. current estimated/mock score.

options.impact: Gives total control to the user but introduces extreme onboarding friction, risking drop-off before the plan is generated.
options.label: Manual Syllabus Configuration: The user manually inputs their own chapters and starting points.

questions.question: How should the student's 'current foundation' (当前基础) be assessed during onboarding to bootstrap the initial plan?
questions.reason: This assessment directly dictates the baseline intensity and starting point of the generated plan; if it is too complex, onboarding friction will be too high; if it is too vague, the generated plan will be inaccurate.
questions.recommendation: Use a simple self-assessment checklist of broad phases (e.g., 'Zero foundation', 'Finished first round of review', 'Doing mock exams') for each selected subject.
questions.recommendation_reason: This provides a fast onboarding experience while offering enough calibration to scale the first month's study intensity.

options.impact: Significantly improves completion tracking accuracy because students can check off tasks in real-time in libraries/classrooms. Minimal scope creep if plan generation and settings remain desktop-only.
options.label: (Recommended) Responsive Mobile-web Checklist: Optimize the task listing and check-off screens for mobile web browsers, keeping all onboarding and plan configuration desktop-only.

options.impact: Keeps the initial build strictly within the defined scope, but risks low user engagement and inaccurate metrics because students must wait to log progress on their computers.
options.label: Strictly Desktop-only Layout: Rely on students logging into a computer at the end of their study day to update their progress.

questions.question: Since students often study in classrooms/libraries without convenient desktop access, should the MVP support a mobile-responsive view solely for checking off tasks?
questions.reason: A strict desktop-only limitation makes real-time logging inconvenient for students studying on the go. This could lead to delayed or forgotten updates, directly impacting the accuracy of your 2-week consecutive completion validation metric.
questions.recommendation: Design a responsive mobile view limited strictly to viewing the daily checklist and marking tasks as complete, while keeping onboarding and planning desktop-only.
questions.recommendation_reason: This fits the user's physical study habits without expanding the MVP to a full mobile planning tool.

risks: Accumulated task debt ('planning debt') causing students to feel overwhelmed and abandon the tool.
High onboarding drop-off if the process of specifying subjects and foundation levels is too tedious or ambiguous.
Under-logging or inaccurate completion metrics due to the friction of only being able to check off tasks when on a desktop browser.

tensions.description: Quiet, mature UI style vs. Completion nudging
tensions.reason: A quiet and non-intrusive calendar/to-do design may lack the visual urgency or notifications needed to prompt students to complete tasks, which is critical for validating the 2-week consecutive completion metric.

tensions.description: Desktop-only MVP vs. Physical study environments
tensions.reason: Postgraduate students study heavily in university libraries, study rooms, or classrooms where laptops may not always be open or convenient for checking off quick daily tasks.

unknowns: The level of task granularity (e.g., hourly schedules, daily study topics, or weekly chapter-level milestones) that the planning engine will generate.
Whether the syllabus content and task generation logic will cover all possible major/professional subjects or focus initially on common public subjects (Politics, English, Math).

assumptions: 假设“内容不能离开用户电脑”的实际意图是：不使用由应用开发者运营的中央服务器存储明文数据，避免隐私泄露，而非绝对禁止任何网络传输。
假设“不用用户做任何设置”的实际意图是：尽可能降低用户的配置成本，例如利用操作系统已有的登录状态（如 iCloud、OneDrive）或极简的一次性配对（如扫码）。
假设知识库主要以文本（Markdown）、图片和常用文档为主，单用户的数据总量通常在 GB 级别以下，适合进行基于文件的同步。
candidates: 方案一：基于本地局域网（LAN）P2P 自动同步（类似 Syncthing）。设备在同一局域网下自动发现并加密传输，数据完全不经过任何云端服务器，但换电脑时两台设备必须同时开机联网。
方案二：基于操作系统原生云盘（如 iCloud / OneDrive）自动同步。将应用数据目录设在系统默认同步文件夹内，配合本地端到端加密（E2EE）确保云端数据不可读。
方案三：基于第三方云存储（如 WebDAV / Object Storage）端到端加密同步。用户在应用内输入自己的云盘密钥，应用自动在后台加密同步。
confirmed: 开发一个个人知识库应用。
应用必须支持完全离线使用，核心功能不依赖网络。
在用户更换电脑时，数据能够自动同步到新电脑。
同步过程对用户而言应当是零配置/免设置的。
conflicts: “完全离线且数据不出电脑”与“自动同步到新电脑”存在物理实现冲突。为了同步，数据必须通过某种介质（网络或物理设备）传输到新电脑，不可能完全不离开原电脑。
“零配置/免设置”与“数据安全与身份校验”存在安全逻辑冲突。如果在新电脑上不需要任何设置或验证（如登录或配对），应用将无法识别用户身份，任何人都可以轻易获取或冒领该用户的加密数据。

gaps.area: 数据同步传输介质与边界
gaps.dependency: 同步方案技术选型
gaps.impact: 决定系统是纯局域网 P2P 架构，还是依赖系统原生云盘，抑或是需要中继服务器。
gaps.reason: 完全离线与换电脑自动同步之间存在根本性的传输矛盾，必须明确“数据不出电脑”的严格定义（是绝对不联网，还是不上传开发者服务器）。

gaps.area: 身份验证与安全加密机制
gaps.dependency: 无感同步体验设计
gaps.impact: 影响同步的安全性。如果追求极端的免设置，可能会牺牲数据安全性；如果要安全，则需要某种首次配对设置。
gaps.reason: 无设置的自动同步难以在多台设备间安全地建立信任关系和解密数据。

gaps.area: 目标运行平台与跨平台范围
gaps.dependency: 开发技术栈选型
gaps.impact: 如果需要跨平台（如 Win 和 Mac 互通），则无法简单依赖 iCloud 等单一平台的免设置同步机制。
gaps.reason: 不同操作系统的免配置同步机制差异巨大，同平台和跨平台的设计难度完全不同。

options.impact: 数据完全不经过云端，但换电脑时需要两台电脑同时开机且在同一局域网，且首次需要扫码配对。
options.label: 使用局域网（LAN）内设备直接 P2P 同步（类似 Syncthing），数据绝不上云。

options.impact: 只要系统登录了云盘账号就能自动同步，且在本地进行端到端加密（E2EE），云端也无法解密，兼顾零设置与隐私。
options.label: (Recommended) 利用我已登录的系统云盘（如 iCloud / OneDrive）进行本地端到端加密同步。

options.impact: 虽然需要手动配置一次账号信息，但对同步媒介和数据存储有完全的掌控力。
options.label: 允许手动配置一次我的私有云（如 WebDAV 或私人云存储）来同步加密数据。

questions.question: 关于“数据不能离开电脑”与“换电脑自动同步”的冲突，您倾向于采用哪种折中方案？
questions.reason: 完全离线且数据不出电脑意味着新电脑无法获取数据。必须在数据传输介质上做出折中。
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) 利用我已登录的系统云盘（如 iCloud / OneDrive）进行本地端到端加密同步。
questions.recommendation_reason: 这样数据虽然离开了物理电脑，但存储在用户自己信任的云盘中，且因为是端到端加密，第三方云服务商和应用开发者都无法读取内容，既实现了换电脑后的“免设置自动同步”，又保证了数据隐私和安全性。

assumptions: The app targets modern web browsers (PWA) as the primary platform to maximize team accessibility and ease of adoption.
A centralized sync server is acceptable to coordinate synchronization, store persistent backups, and manage user identity.
Users require a rich text editing interface (e.g. lists, headings, formatting) rather than plain text or markdown.
Media files (images/attachments) are secondary to text synchronization and can be handled via lazy uploading/downloading once online.
candidates: Yjs + TipTap/ProseMirror (CRDT-based rich text editor with real-time and offline collaborative sync)
Automerge + custom document editor (JSON-based document CRDT)
Electric SQL / RxDB / Replicache (Local-first relational/document database synchronization engines)
Git-like branching and manual merge reconciliation for notes/sections
confirmed: Local-first architecture: The application must store and manage data locally by default.
Offline editing: Team members must be able to create, view, and edit notes without an active internet connection.
Automatic merge on reconnect: Notes must sync and merge automatically once a network connection is recovered.
Overwrite prevention: The system must prevent team members' edits from easily overwriting each other when merging.
Domain focus: Team meeting notes.
conflicts: Offline Collaboration vs Identity/Permissions: Collaborative editing requires knowing who edited what to enforce permissions, but offline-first means authorization status cannot be validated against a server in real-time.

Automatic Character-Level Merging vs User Intent: While CRDTs automatically merge changes to avoid manual conflicts, overlapping edits can still lead to semantic gibberish or logical conflicts (e.g., duplicated action items) that technically 'overwrite' or disrupt a user's intent.

gaps.dependency: CRDT vs Database Sync Engine selection
gaps.impact: Directly determines the feasibility of the 'cannot easily overwrite others' changes' requirement.
gaps.reason: CRDTs (Yjs) allow real-time character-level merging, whereas local-first DB sync (Replicache/RxDB) works at the document/row level. This choice dictates the entire tech stack.

gaps.dependency: Platform-specific storage and file system APIs
gaps.impact: Affects storage persistence guarantees (IndexedDB can be cleared by browsers, native SQLite/OPFS is more persistent).
gaps.reason: We need to know whether to build a Web App (PWA) or a Desktop App (Tauri) for local-first storage persistence.

gaps.dependency: User session persistence when offline
gaps.impact: Affects permission checks and edit history tracking when offline.
gaps.reason: If a user is offline, they cannot authenticate with a remote OAuth provider. We need a way to sign in / identify users offline.

questions.question: 为了确保首个版本的安全性和快速上线，我们是否可以先专注于单一核心平台（例如浏览器插件）并配合云端同步，而不是在首发时同时支持 Windows、浏览器插件和手机？
questions.reason: 密码管理器对安全性要求极高。同时开发和审计 Windows 客户端、浏览器插件和移动端 APP，会极大增加开发周期并带来更多潜在的安全漏洞面。先验证一个平台可以确保核心加密和同步机制足够稳固。
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) 优先开发浏览器插件作为 MVP 的首发平台，并提供云端同步能力。
questions.recommendation_reason: 浏览器插件是用户使用密码管理器和自动填充功能最频繁的场景，开发成本相对较低，能最快为用户提供核心价值，同时便于迭代和安全验证。

options.impact: 用户体验最流畅，安全性极高，但如果用户丢失主密码且未备份恢复密钥，数据将永久丢失。
options.label: (Recommended) 零知识加密云同步：数据在用户本地加密后上传到托管云端，仅用户持有主密码，云端无法解密任何内容。

options.impact: 用户对数据有完全的控制权，无需信任第三方密码管理服务商，但配置门槛较高，同步体验可能不够顺畅。
options.label: 本地优先/用户自备云同步：数据保存在本地，通过本地局域网或用户自备的第三方云存储进行同步。

options.impact: 降低了用户因遗忘密码而丢失数据的风险，但意味着服务商在特定情况下能协助重置/获取解密路径，无法做到绝对的零知识隐私。
options.label: 传统云同步：数据加密存储在云端，但提供受限的安全恢复通道（如通过绑定的安全邮箱/手机找回密码）。

questions.question: 在跨设备同步时，您倾向于采用哪种数据存储与隐私控制方案？
questions.reason: 这决定了产品的安全架构设计和用户的信任基础。不同的同步策略会直接影响到用户对隐私的掌控程度以及是否需要自备存储空间。
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) 采用零知识加密（Zero-Knowledge）云同步方案。
questions.recommendation_reason: 这是目前主流安全密码管理器的标准做法。数据在本地加密后再同步，服务商无法查看内容，兼顾了多端同步的便利性和极高的隐私安全性。

risks: 若同步时的加密实现或密钥管理不当，可能导致用户凭证在传输/存储中泄露。
若用户遗忘主密码且没有本地备份/紧急恢复密钥，会导致数据永久丢失。
自动填充机制若存在漏洞，可能会被恶意网页或跨站脚本（XSS）钓鱼窃取凭证。
多设备同时修改数据时可能产生同步冲突，导致用户最新修改的内容被覆盖。

tensions.description: 跨设备便捷同步与零知识隐私控制之间的权衡
